item.research_question: How do native oxidation, lattice distortion, and the resulting core–shell microstructure influence the ferromagnetism, saturation magnetization, coercivity, and electrical resistivity of CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy thin films?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNi thin films (CoCrFeNithin, CoCrFeNithick), AlxCoCrFeNi (x = 0.1–0.5), and CoCrFeNiOx (x = 0.4, 0.8) high-entropy alloy thin films
item.processing_route: Radio frequency (RF) magnetron sputtering on single-crystal Si (100) substrates; background vacuum < 3.0 × 10−4 Pa; substrate temperature ≤ 323 K; Ar pressure ≈ 1.4 Pa (30 sccm); RF power 100–110 W; native oxidation occurred during/after deposition; O-incorporated films prepared with O2/Ar mixture at 0.3 Pa working pressure
item.test_conditions: Room temperature (298 K); in-plane magnetic hysteresis loops measured by vibrating sample magnetometer; electrical resistivity measured by four-point probe; microstructure and composition analyzed by SEM, TEM, XRD, EPMA, EDS-TEM, APT, and XPS; magnetic domains imaged by magnetic force microscopy
key_findings: CoCrFeNithick film achieved a saturation magnetization (MS) of 667 emu cm−3 and a coercivity (HC) of 0.12 kA m−1, while CoCrFeNithin film showed MS = 445 emu cm−3 and HC = 1.55 kA m−1.
O-incorporated CoCrFeNiO0.4 film exhibited an electrical resistivity of 237 µΩ·cm, MS of 535 emu cm−3, and HC of 23 A m−1.
The CoCrFeNithick film displayed the highest initial permeability (µi = 466), whereas AlxCoCrFeNi films showed µi decreasing to 27 with increasing Al concentration.
Native oxidation created a core–shell structure where ferromagnetic Fe, Co, and Ni form the core and Cr oxide acts as a shell layer around columnar crystals.
The electrical resistivity of CoCrFeNithin (335.0 ± 2.09 µΩ·cm) was significantly higher than that of CoCrFeNithick (153.0 ± 4.52 µΩ·cm) due to increased grain boundaries and microcracks.
The FCC phase in the films exhibited ferromagnetism at room temperature due to severe lattice distortion, contrary to the paramagnetic behavior of bulk FCC CoCrFeNi alloys.
Magnetic domain sizes in CoCrFeNithick film were ≈65 nm, smaller than the ≈90 nm domains observed in other films.
item.mechanism: Ferromagnetism arises from severe lattice distortion in the non-equilibrium thin films, which alters the exchange interaction distance (d–δ) to weaken antiferromagnetic Cr–Cr interactions and strengthen ferromagnetic Fe–Fe, Co–Co, and Ni–Ni interactions in the FCC phase. The native oxidation of Cr creates a core–shell structure that further enhances ferromagnetism by reducing Cr–Cr pairs, introducing ferromagnetic Cr–O–Cr interactions, and increasing the concentration of ferromagnetic elements in the core. Coercivity is dominated by complex magnetic anisotropy (macroscopic shape, columnar crystal, magneto-crystalline, and stress anisotropy) and is inversely related to magnetic domain size and the ratio of anisotropy energy to saturation magnetization (EA/MS).
item.limitations: The text notes that theoretical results for bulk HEAs cannot be directly applied to HEATFs due to differences in coordination numbers, lattice constants, and valence electron distributions. Additionally, residual stress generated during fabrication significantly affects magnetic properties, and the presence of microcracks in thinner films increases coercivity.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the films can be employed to develop soft magnetic electronic devices due to their large composition- and performance-modulation ranges, and suggest that the native oxidation mechanism could be further explored to optimize composite effects.
quotes: The core–shell structure enables a high saturation magnetization, enhances the electrical resistivity, and thus reduces the eddy‐current loss.
The ferromagnetism source can then be determined by considering the following three aspects in the current CoCrFeNi‐based HEATFs.

item.research_question: How do native oxidation and the addition of Al or O affect the soft magnetic properties and electrical resistivity of CoCrFeNi-based high-entropy alloy thin films?
item.material_system: CoCrFeNi-based HEATFs, specifically CoCrFeNi and CoCrFeNiO0.4, with variations involving Al and O additions
item.processing_route: Preparation of soft magnetic CoCrFeNi thin films with FCC and BCC dual-phases via a method resulting in native oxidation
key_findings: CoCrFeNiO0.4 film exhibited an electrical resistivity of 237 µΩ·cm
CoCrFeNiO0.4 film showed a saturation magnetization of 535 emu cm−3
CoCrFeNiO0.4 film demonstrated a coercivity of 23 A m−1
Addition of O increases both electrical resistivity (ρ) and saturation magnetization/coercivity (MS/HC)
Addition of Al appropriately increases ρ but slightly reduces MS/HC
The films possess a native oxidation-produced core–shell structure with a ferromagnetic core (Fe, Co, Ni) and a Cr oxide shell
item.mechanism: The ferromagnetism is determined by reinforced exchange interaction due to lattice distortion, weakened antiferromagnetic exchange due to preferential Cr oxidation, and contribution from the BCC phase; coercivity is associated with complex magnetic anisotropy and domain wall sizes; preferential Cr oxidation promotes the core–shell structure, adjusting the ratio between ferromagnetic and high-resistivity phases
item.limitations: A detailed study on the evaluation of the effect of O addition on the soft magnetic properties is ongoing, and the corresponding results will be reported in the future
item.future_work: A detailed study on the evaluation of the effect of O addition on the soft magnetic properties is ongoing, and the corresponding results will be reported in the future
quotes: The CoCrFeNiO0.4 film showed the best properties, with an electrical resistivity of 237 µΩ·cm, a saturation magnetization of 535 emu cm−3 and a coercivity of 23 A m−1.
The films showed a native oxidation‐produced core–shell structure, which comprised a core formed by the ferromagnetic elements Fe, Co, and Ni and a shell layer formed by the Cr oxide.

The preferential oxidation of Cr can promote the formation of the aforementioned core–shell structure, and adjust the content ratio between the phase with ferromagnetism and that with a high electrical resistivity and weak magnetism to obtain optimized soft magnetic properties.
